# Type arrivals

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

How words come on: rises, snaps, decodes, focus pulls, typing and letter builds, each with its own curve and cadence. 69 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Giant word rises in, cropped by the frame

`dv-giant-cropped-rise` · opening hooks · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, sting, vertical

One word so large the frame crops it (cap height 31-55 % of the frame) rises or drops into place on a steep expo-out; often the layout pans at the same time, so the path is a J-shaped swoop, or the product swaps underneath it.

- **Build:** <Words> at display size with rise 0.8-1 em and dur 20-60 on E.snapOut inside a cropping frame; stepped variant inside <Stepped fps={16}>; the band is a LightSweep clipped to the text. Anatomy: A single display word at 3-6x body size; rise 330-740 px; variants: on every third frame held (stepped); with the whole layout panning left as it rises; dropping from above while a one-hue band about 1.5 letters wide travels through the letters. Sound: A spacebar-like click, or sub-bass plus kick when the product swaps under it.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** 17-60 f expo-out (tau about 15 f); pan 55 f on 16 fps steps; band crosses in 16 f.
- **Use when:** Opening a film or a section with one word; a word that rides over a product shot.
- **Avoid when:** Words whose meaning depends on the cropped letters.

### Centre-out line unmask

`ty-centre-out-unmask` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough, launch, loop

A short line opens from its own centre outward behind a soft-edged mask while the letters stay perfectly still, so a result or status reads as unveiled rather than flown in.

- **Build:** Lay out the final centred line, get its width w from measureTracked, and keep every glyph static. Reveal it with a horizontal mask on the line box: o = w x prog(f, s, s + 18, E.out), and mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent (50% - o/2 - 20px), #000 (50% - o/2), #000 (50% + o/2), transparent (50% + o/2 + 20px)), computed in px each frame, so both edges travel outward with a 20 px feather (a hard clip-path: inset(0 calc(50% - o/2)) is fine inside a pill). Over the same window, run opacity 0.6 -> 1 and letter-spacing +0.04 em -> the token's tracking on E.out, so the line tightens as it opens. Set it under a centred icon or check that has just landed, starting 4-6 f after the icon's landing frame; for a second line, open it 6 f after the first. Keep the hold alive with a drift of at most 0.3 px/f, and exit with the whole line over 12 f on E.smooth or with ty-reading-order-exit.
- **Timing:** Unmask over 18 f on E.out (31% of each half-width opens on frame 1), with a 20 px feather. Opacity 0.6 -> 1 and tracking +0.04 em -> token over the same 18 f. Starts 4-6 f after the icon lands; a second line follows at +6 f. Hold at least 36 f + 6 f per word, drifting at most 0.3 px/f. Exit over 12 f on E.smooth.
- **Use when:** A result, status or confirmation line under a centred icon ('Published', 'Connected'). A hero word inside a pill that has just formed. A calm sub-line under a headline that has already landed.
- **Avoid when:** Lines over about 40 characters (the edges take too long to reach the ends). Left-aligned layouts (wipe from the left edge instead). Text that is also moving, where the mask fights the glyph motion. Headlines that need energy.

### Cut on low at full ink, slide home

`dv-pop-low-slide` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy medium · any

A word cuts on at full opacity a little below (or beside) its slot and slides home on an exponential, so the first frame is a clean hit and the motion is pure settle.

- **Build:** <Words dur={1} rise={0.45} riseUnit="em" riseDur={22} riseEase={E.snapOut} stagger={5}>; for a side entry rotate the rise direction. Anatomy: Opacity 1 from frame one; offset 0.27-0.45 of the cap height (18-56 px at 1080p) below or 66 px to the right; variant: two linear frames of 104 px before the expo tail for a word that must travel far (259 px); variant: slide left until it touches the previous word. Sound: Each word on a kick or a soft tick; a run of words gets one sound.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** Settle 10-38 f expo-out; stagger 2-5 f; a far travel uses 2 linear frames then 20 f expo.
- **Use when:** Punchier copy on a beat, headline words on a coloured field, a word that should touch the one before it.
- **Avoid when:** Very large type (the cut-on jump reads as a glitch above about 60 px of offset).

### Fade-and-rise word, front-loaded

`dv-word-fade-rise` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy calm · any

The default way a word arrives: it is already a third visible on its first frame and rises a third of its line box as it fades, so it reads as present at once and lands softly.

- **Build:** <Words> at house numbers (dur 32, rise 0.33 line, stagger 12, cadence 'reading'); a drop uses riseDir up with a 2-frame vertical ghost; a diagonal entry offsets x by 1.2x the rise. Anatomy: One tween per word on opacity (from about 35 %) and y (0.2-0.8 em, house 0.33 line box). Variants: a drop from above with a short vertical smear for an energetic headline; a diagonal entry (from 54 px low and 68 px right) for a new line that rides a camera move; a second word starting one frame after the first on the same curve so a two-word opener reads as one object. Sound: Words sit on voice onsets; with no voice, one soft tick per fragment on the last word's landing, never one per word. Materials: Floor-reflection variant: each word rises into place trailing a faded, vertically flipped copy under it (blur 1 px, 40 % decaying to 0 in 8 f) as if it rose out of a glossy floor, the word itself going from 50 to 100 % white.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Materials:** Floor-reflection variant: each word rises into place trailing a faded, vertically flipped copy under it (blur 1 px, 40 % decaying to 0 in 8 f) as if it rose out of a glossy floor, the word itself going from 50 to 100 % white.
- **Timing:** Fade 32 f on a steep ease-out (50 % at 10 % of the time, 90 % by 15 f), rise 22-25 f. Stagger 8-14 f on a reading cadence; 2 f for a two-word opener; 8-14 f for a voice-clocked caption. Travel 23-77 px at 1080p.
- **Use when:** Any calm statement, voice-clocked captions, the body copy of a launch or update film.
- **Avoid when:** A beat that needs a hit (use a pop or an oversized landing), or a line already moving with the camera.

### In-place ink-up from partial strength

`dv-ink-in-place` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy calm · any

Words or rows appear exactly in their final place, already 29-60 % strong on the first frame, and ink up to full with no movement at all; several words are often mid-fade together.

- **Build:** <Words rise={0} dur={20} stagger={8}> with the first-frame strength set by the ease (E.snapOut gives about 35 %); colour-from-tint via accent = the panel tint and accentHold 0. Anatomy: Opacity only (or a colour from the panel tint or a light grey to the ink). Variants: words land grey and snap to full ink on the frame the next word lands (the recency snap); data rows dim then bright 1-2 f apart; pairs of two words at a time for small UI copy; side words fading in 7 f after a hit. Sound: Key or click ticks on word onsets for a typed feel, otherwise none.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** First frame 29-60 % (house 38 %); 90 % by 10-20 f, full by 20-32 f on an expo-out. Stagger 4-12 f per word; lines 5-8 f apart; rows 2-4 f apart; a recency snap is one frame.
- **Use when:** Dense layouts (a page, a card, data rows, captions on photos) where motion would fight the layout, and small UI copy.
- **Avoid when:** A hero line that needs energy; long lines that would all be half-inked at once.

### In-place word light-up on beats

`ty-inplace-light-up-beats` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough, vertical

The finished line is laid out from the start and its words light up in place, chunk by chunk on the beat, with the last word held back.

- **Build:** Lay out the final centred line once; every word is a span at its final position with opacity 0, so nothing ever reflows. Group the words into 2-3 chunks that start on beat frames, 6 f apart within a chunk; each word's opacity is tw(f, s, s + 5, 0, 0.75, E.linear) then rises to 1 over the next 40 f on E.outSoft (fast attack, slow brightening tail). Hierarchy without a second colour: keywords at weight 600, connectors at 400 held at 0.55 until the last chunk lands and then raised to 1 over 12 f; the final word or qualifier arrives a full beat late, and a qualifier may sit tucked under the line's right edge at 0.35x size. Across a film, shorten the per-word stagger from 24 f on the title to about 6 f on later captions, because viewers learn the pattern; exit the whole line at once.
- **Timing:** Attack 5 f to 0.75, tail 40 f E.outSoft to 1; 6 f within a chunk, chunks on beats; last token +24-34 f; connectors 0.55 -> 1 over 12 f; title stagger 24 f shrinking to 5-6 f; exit all words together over 26 f E.smooth. If the camera is locked, add a 0.3 px/f line drift.
- **Use when:** Titles and walkthrough captions over a moving camera; lines with an inline glyph or partner wordmark that must not shift; music-led films where each chunk can sit on a beat.
- **Avoid when:** High-energy acts that need motion in the type itself; lines over 6 words (it turns into a slide).

### Line whose stagger and fade shrink word by word

`dv-accelerating-cadence` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy medium · any

Each later word starts sooner and fades faster than the one before, so the line gathers speed into its payoff (often the brand name).

- **Build:** <Words cadence="accelerate" accelTo={0.4}>. Anatomy: Geometric gaps (0.30, 0.23, 0.13, 0.10 s), fades shortening with them; variant: words cut on and slide only their last 10-12 px. Sound: A stab on word 1; or none.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** Gaps 18 -> 6 f at 60 fps; second line fades 12 f with 6-8 f stagger.
- **Use when:** A payoff line, the last line of an act.
- **Avoid when:** Every line (one accelerating run per act).

### Line written on behind a soft moving edge

`dv-soft-edge-write-on` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy calm · any

A line is revealed left to right by a travelling edge about one letter soft, near-constant speed, so it writes on; glyphs can be born in a hot accent and cool; a status line can end with a spinner turning into a check.

- **Build:** <Wipe kind="gradient" feather={about 1.1 em in px} span={the line's width}> on the line (give the edge: the gradient's house edge, 0.7 of the span, is the long ramp); accent via HueSweep or Words accent. Anatomy: an alpha edge of about 1 em (1.2 em at most) and the letters behind it at full strength; glyphs accent -> ink as the edge passes. A long ramp from the ink into the ground (a third of the line or more) reads as half-faded words, never as writing. Sound: a soft notification ding mid-reveal, or a kick at the end. As one line: the TypeLine preset `develop` (a 1.1 em edge in the tint, then the accent and the ink).
- **Primitive:** `fx/Wipe.Wipe`, `fx/TypePresets.TypeLine`
- **Timing:** 6-24 f across 880 px (first 4 f slower); fall-off 56 f.
- **Use when:** Status lines, single lines over a picture.
- **Avoid when:** Edges narrower than a letter (that reads as a hard wipe); edges wider than a word (fade soup); a hero line.

### Masked rise that stops dead

`ty-masked-baseline-rise` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy medium · any

Each word rises out of a mask under its baseline on a near-linear head and stops dead, darkening from a light grey as it rises; the last word takes its time.

- **Build:** <MaskRise text by="word" ink={{ from }} /> with a 1.2 pace: head 10 f@60 (85 % of the rise), the rest on the next frame and a quiet tail; the last word x2.8; starts[] puts words on voice onsets. With an explicit ease or a 1.1 pace the 1.1 rise is kept. As one line: `<TypeLine spec={{ preset: 'mask', text, at }}>` (an 8 f linear-stop head over 1.05 em, words 8 f apart, the last 2.5x, mute to ink as it rises, a mask edge fixed in the line).
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypePresets.TypeLine`, `fx/MaskRise`
- **Timing:** 5 f@30 a word, 3-6 f@30 apart; the last word about 14 f@30.
- **Use when:** A statement read on a voice or a beat, word by word, with a firm landing.
- **Avoid when:** Soft, floating moods (use the canonical reveal).

### Staggered word roll

`ty-staggered-word-roll` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy medium · any

The words of a phrase roll up and away one after another while their replacements rise in from below, so one sentence mutates instead of cutting.

- **Build:** For slot i, t_i = t0 + 10i. Out: q = prog(f, t_i, t_i + 12, E.in), translateY = -depart(q) x 0.2 em, opacity = 1 - prog(f, t_i, t_i + 12, E.smooth), blur = blurOut(q, 6). In, starting at t_i + 4 (a 4 f overlap): p = prog(f, t_i + 4, t_i + 28, E.out), translateY = (1 - arrive(p)) x 0.25 em, opacity 0 -> 1 over 10 f, blur = blurIn(p, 8). Keep any shared element (an icon pill, an unchanged word) perfectly still as the anchor, always roll in the same direction, and re-centre on SPR.firm when the new words change the width.
- **Timing:** Out 12 f E.in, 0.2 em up; in 24 f E.out from +0.25 em (peak about 7 px/f at 120 px type), 4 f overlap; stagger 6-11 f per word; a phrase swap takes about 50 f; a whole-line conveyor variant leaves exactly 1 empty frame between the lines.
- **Use when:** Swapping one claim for the next in place; a URL replacing a tagline; a category word turning into the product name; a closing bookend that rolls the opening phrase into the brand line.
- **Avoid when:** Swaps where nothing persists (a cut or ty-blur-swap-rescale reads cleaner); more than two rolls in a row without a different move between them.

### Typing with a grammar

`ty-typeon-timeboxed` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch, vertical

What the product types types the way it would: a person at 30 a second with bursts and pauses, a field word by word with a one-frame accent, a prompt that speeds up and slows on its last word, a stream at 50-150 a second; cut into it half to four fifths typed.

- **Build:** <TypeOn text kind="human" /> (30 cps runs, comma beats, a breath before the last word, a stop before the closing ? . !); kind="field" accent={C.accent} (a word every 5 f@60, accent one frame); kind="prompt" (5 -> 19 cps over 12 keys, last word x1.6; gaps={ACCEL.typing} into a whip; skip for keys hidden by a move); kind="stream" (100 cps; ease={E.type} to settle); from={0.6} to cut in mid-typing; trail for a colour wake. typeSchedule() gives the key frames for sound and a caret-following camera (typeOn().followX).
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeOn.TypeOn`
- **Timing:** A person 19-30 cps overall; a prompt 1-2 s; a stream under a second; hold the finished string >= 72 f@60.
- **Use when:** A prompt, a search, a command, a reply in a product moment.
- **Avoid when:** Headlines and film copy (they arrive as fragments).

### Typing with an accent trail on the newest characters

`dv-typing-colour-trail` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy calm · any

While text types or streams, its newest characters (or words) wear the accent and age to ink behind the caret: a colour trail that shows where the writing is.

- **Build:** <TypeOn kind="human"|"stream" trail={{ color: C.accent, chars: 10 }}>; a mention is a span with its own colour. Anatomy: Trail of 6-12 characters (about 600 px) fading accent -> ink; variants: the last 2-4 characters grey on a pale highlight block (typing in word bursts); a streamed answer with a grey leading tail; a mention token that types in its own colour and keeps it; a pink caret matching the trail. Sound: Keypress ticks for a person; none for a machine stream; a chat pop when a mention completes. Materials: A colour wave runs through the typed answer behind the caret: once about 8 characters exist a band about 5 characters wide (the accent at the centre, soft to white over 2 characters each side) starts at the first letter and travels more slowly than the typing (0.75 of its speed), so it ends after the typing does.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeOn`
- **Materials:** A colour wave runs through the typed answer behind the caret: once about 8 characters exist a band about 5 characters wide (the accent at the centre, soft to white over 2 characters each side) starts at the first letter and travels more slowly than the typing (0.75 of its speed), so it ends after the typing does.
- **Timing:** 24-90 characters a second; word bursts every 6 f; streams at about 30 words a second; trail ages over 10 characters.
- **Use when:** Prompts, AI answers, streamed replies, any product typing.
- **Avoid when:** Two accents at once; trails longer than about 12 characters.

### Word comes into focus

`ty-blur-focus-word-rise` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough, vertical · also `dv-focus-in-word`

A word shows soft and a little to the side on its first frame and slides home while the defocus falls away in three frames, so it lands sharp, not faded in.

- **Build:** <FocusWord text start mode="word" /> or focusIn on Chain / Words. House: sigma 4.6 px at 1080p falling to 0.41 of itself a frame at 30 fps (sharp from the fourth frame), slide 55 px on M.focusSlide over 7 f@30. Drawn as at most two fixed ladder copies, never an animated blur radius. Product strings: mode="ui", parts split on '|', 0/+2/+5/+6/+10 f@60, 10 f each, contrast snapping in late.
- **Primitive:** `fx/FocusWord`, `fx/Chain`, `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** 3-7 frames at 30 fps; UI parts 10-16 f@60 each.
- **Use when:** A keyword that should feel like it was found; a UI string resolving as the camera lands.
- **Avoid when:** Running copy (it slows the read); type under 36 px.

### Word rises out of a baseline mask

`dv-mask-rise-word` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy medium · any

Each word rises from behind an invisible baseline mask while going grey to ink; the last word takes twice as long; verb-plus-object lines can follow with a 3 f lag.

- **Build:** <MaskRise lastScale={2} ink>. Anatomy: Rise of about 90 px from under the baseline, ink from grey; variant: staggered hard exit. Sound: Hits on each verb. As one line: the TypeLine preset `mask`.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypePresets.TypeLine`, `fx/MaskRise`
- **Timing:** Rise 18-20 f; second word 6 f behind; exit 14 f; lines 60 f apart.
- **Use when:** Short commands, verbs on hits, any line that should feel cut and precise.
- **Avoid when:** Long lines (the masked rise loses its snap).

### Words drop into the line from above

`ty-drop-from-above` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy any · any

Each word drops a short way into its slot from above, from a muted grey to the ink, trailing a short vertical smear; the last word lands in the accent and cools.

- **Build:** Word w starts at at + 9w f; p = prog(f, o, o + 12, E.snapOut); translateY = -0.28 em x (1 - p); opacity = 0.4 + 0.6p; colour mixColor(mute, ink, p); a smear of 0.12 em x (1 - p) above it (two or three fading copies). The last word mixes toward the accent instead and cools to the ink over 30 f after it lands. As one line: `<TypeLine spec={{ preset: 'fall', text, at }}>`.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypePresets.TypeLine`
- **Timing:** Per word 12 f, 9 f apart (8-10), drop 0.28 em (0.2-0.3); a four-word line lands in about 40 f.
- **Use when:** A line over a dark, deep ground (a product world, a night UI) where a rise from below would fight the composition; a claim that settles down onto the product.
- **Avoid when:** Two lines in a row that both drop; a light, airy film where the canonical rise is the voice.

### Words spill out from behind a mark

`ty-occlusion-spill-from-mark` · typography in motion · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

A glyph or icon slides aside and the words shoot out from behind it, clipped at its edge, as if the mark were delivering the message.

- **Build:** Put the words in a container clipped at the mark's current edge (for a leftward spill, clip-path: inset(0 calc(100% - (markX - boxLeft)) 0 0)) and draw the mark above them. Mark: translateX 0 -> +260 px on prog(f, s, s + 20, E.out); words: translateX +320 -> 0 on p = prog(f, s + 1, s + 25, E.out) with blurIn(p, 8) and opacity 0 -> 1 over 6 f, hidden behind the mark at first and readable once they drop below 20 px/f around frame 6. Inline variant: an icon shrinks (lmix 3 -> 1, optionally tilting in 3D) into the bullet slot at the start of a sentence and the words slide out to its right from behind it the same way.
- **Timing:** Mark 260 px over 20 f E.out (peak about 73 px/f, blurred master); words 320 px over 24 f E.out (76 px/f on frame 1, under 20 by frame 6), 1 f after the mark; opacity 6 f; hold at least 54 f with a drift.
- **Use when:** An icon-led claim mid-film, or an opening line pushed out by the mark already in motion; a feature icon that introduces its own line; a mark or number that says the sentence.
- **Avoid when:** The end lockup (it appears once and belongs to the end card); marks smaller than the cap height (nothing to hide behind); spills longer than about 360 px.

### A highlight walks the line, parks on the keyword, new words type hot

`dv-highlight-walk-park` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

A grey line lights up in the accent as a whole, then the colour narrows to a window that walks word by word and parks on the keyword; new words then type in, each born in the accent and cooling to grey, while the keyword keeps its colour.

- **Build:** Recipe: word spans with a colour state per frame (the window index from the clock), then TypeOn for the continuation with a per-character cool. Anatomy: Whole-line flash 8 f; the window steps about every 8 f; park 24 f; typing about one character per 2 f with word-end pauses; typed letters cool accent -> grey over 12 f; every colour change is a linear lerp over 12-16 f, never a cut. Sound: None needed.
- **Timing:** About 90 f for the whole move.
- **Use when:** A line inside a UI (a subtitle, a result) that carries the claim; two colours only.
- **Avoid when:** Big display copy (use a tint wave or an ink path).

### A label rises in gradient ink, then a blink wave turns it white

`dv-tinted-then-white-blink` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

A small label rises from a baseline mask filled with the same gradient as the card behind it, so it is almost camouflaged; then a wave passes left to right: each letter blinks out for a few frames and comes back pure white, so for a moment the word reads white, gap, tinted.

- **Build:** Recipe: MaskRise for the rise, then per-letter spans whose fill switches from the gradient clip to white after a 4 f dropout. Anatomy: Rise 12 f; tinted hold 16 f (text clipped to the card's gradient at about 0.8); dropout wave about 4 f apart per letter, each letter off for 4 f, then white. Sound: A soft tick per letter, or none.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeFx.GradientText`
- **Timing:** About 76 f in all.
- **Use when:** A label on a gradient or tinted card; a product name inside a UI card.
- **Avoid when:** Long copy; plain grounds (the camouflage needs the gradient behind).

### Glyph scramble that locks into the word

`dv-glyph-scramble-lock` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

Random glyphs (letters, digits, symbols) cycle in each slot and lock into the word, left to right or out of order, with exactly one accent glyph at a time; a sentence can scramble out the same way.

- **Build:** <Scramble rateHz={10} order="ltr"> (or 'random'); accent glyph via the accent prop; declares the span stepped. Anatomy: Per slot 10 changes a second, locking in order; one glyph in the accent; variants: arrow or symbol glyphs decoding into a wordmark, each new letter accent first then all ink; a sentence dropping out to random glyphs while the title resolves in the accent and flips to ink. Sound: A UI pop on the scramble's start; the title can land in a stop-down silence. Materials: Two constructions. Halo scramble: the word cycles through whole random glyph sets, each held exactly 6 f (10 Hz), inside a soft white halo (a blurred copy at 20 px, 45 %, screen) with the scrambling accent glyphs carrying a smaller accent glow; the halo switches off on the lock frame as a cut, while the word settles from 1.2x to 1.0. Positional scramble: letters keep their slots, random letters drop out, foreign glyphs and ligatures appear in the gaps, then the new string resolves through a pale tint for one state before the ink (about 4 f per state).
- **Primitive:** `fx/Scramble`
- **Materials:** Two constructions. Halo scramble: the word cycles through whole random glyph sets, each held exactly 6 f (10 Hz), inside a soft white halo (a blurred copy at 20 px, 45 %, screen) with the scrambling accent glyphs carrying a smaller accent glow; the halo switches off on the lock frame as a cut, while the word settles from 1.2x to 1.0. Positional scramble: letters keep their slots, random letters drop out, foreign glyphs and ligatures appear in the gaps, then the new string resolves through a pale tint for one state before the ink (about 4 f per state).
- **Timing:** A state every 6 f (10 Hz); 7 states over 38 f; decode out 13 f, in 10 f, colour flip 1 f.
- **Use when:** A product name, a code, a version, a title once per film.
- **Avoid when:** Running copy; more than once per film.

### Handwritten line writes on at pen speed

`dv-signature-write-on` · typography in motion · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

A monoline handwritten signature draws left to right at a constant pen speed on a card; it can write twice as cards swap.

- **Build:** SVG path with stroke-dashoffset from strokeDrawn() (65 px a frame at 60 fps) or a linear tween. Anatomy: One SVG stroke, dash offset at constant speed. Sound: A soft pen scratch.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Stepped.strokeDrawn`
- **Timing:** 52-67 f linear per write; card swap 37 f overlapping by 12 f.
- **Use when:** Personal, signed, approved moments.
- **Avoid when:** Fonts pretending to be handwriting.

### Hard-step edits that act out the copy

`ty-step-edit-performs-copy` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

The headline does what it says with one-frame edits: broken words click straight one at a time, or words delete from the end faster and faster.

- **Build:** Give each word two states and pick one by fd(f) >= step_i, with no tween at all. Fix variant: broken states are per-letter rotation along an arc (letter j rotated (j - mid) x 6 degrees and raised (j - mid)^2 x 2 px), skewX(15deg) with translateY -0.17 em, or rotate(-20deg), drifting 0.5 px/f while broken; steps land at +6, +26 and +40 f after the cut, each with a 2% scale punch from hitPulse(t, 1, 4) on the fixed word. Delete variant: words.slice(0, n) with n dropping at accelerating intervals (10, 5, 5, 2 f), building pressure into the cut. Each step gets one click, each a little louder than the last.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Keep only the rotation-based broken states (letters fanned along an arc, or the word rotated -20 deg) and drop the skewX(15deg) state, which fakes an italic; the one-frame steps, the 2% punches and the accelerating deletes stay as they are. The full look relies on italic; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Snap 1 f, no tween; fix intervals 20 then 14 f; delete intervals 10/5/5/2 f; broken-state drift 0.5 px/f; click within 1 f of each step; hold the fixed line at least 42 f.
- **Use when:** Copy about fixing, undoing, cleaning up or simplifying; a deadpan joke beat; a problem line that should visibly go away.
- **Avoid when:** Copy the motion would contradict; calm films; more than one per film.

### Keyword inks along one hue

`ty-front-restyle-sweep` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting · also `dv-sweep-set-line`

A keyword arrives pale, holds its lightness while its colour turns, then darkens through the accent to the ink; the end of the word leads by a step.

- **Build:** <HueSweep text start /> (or sweep on Chain / Words): the house one-hue sweep at the accent's hue, lightness near L .86 for a third, then an ease-in to the ink; chroma swells to the accent (at most C .12, kept inside sRGB) just past half-way. 9 f@30 a word, words 10-12 f@30 apart, the right end leading by 0.5 f a letter. A brand may pass its own path; multi-hue paths are the generated look.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** A one-hue front (mute -> accent -> ink per glyph through mixColor) instead of a multi-hue band, and a variable-weight wave (400 -> 700) in the film's one sans instead of switching glyphs to a serif italic. The full look relies on gradient, serif, italic; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Primitive:** `fx/HueSweep`, `fx/Chain`, `fx/Words`
- **Materials:** The sentence develops through several hues before it settles: a transparent head (feathered about 5 letters) followed by fronts of peach, pink, lilac and blue, each slower than the one before, so mid-move the line shows several hues at once; the ink front eases out (power about 2.1) and stalls at 85 % of the line before the end catches up. Reveal head about 1.2 letters per drawing (44 f to the end), the blue front about 120 f, the ink 260 f.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** 0.3 s a word; a phrase of 2-4 words over about a second.
- **Use when:** The one keyword of a statement; a version number or a product name.
- **Avoid when:** Several hues (unless the brand supplies them); whole sentences.

### Letter spacing snaps to normal

`dv-tracking-snap` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

A word appears too tight (letters overlapping) or too loose and snaps or tracks in to its normal spacing.

- **Build:** <Letters tracking> (house +0.024 em closing over 20 f) or Wordmark trackingState. Anatomy: Tracking from 78-83 % or 102-128 % of the word's width to 100 %, on 16 fps steps or an ease-out. Sound: The hard cut.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Letters`
- **Timing:** 8-15 f on steps; a slow track-in 20 f.
- **Use when:** Words on cards in a fast cut sequence; a small subtitle settling under a figure.
- **Avoid when:** Long sentences.

### Letter-by-letter fade across a word

`dv-letter-fade-sweep` · typography in motion · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

A word fades in letter by letter from left to right, about one letter a frame, each with a short fade; trailing letters can rise in one at a time while the line moves.

- **Build:** <Letters mode="pop"> (rise 0.19 em) or build. Anatomy: Each letter a 4-8 f fade (and optionally a 60 px rise at 50 % white); 1-2 f apart. Sound: A water-drop on the start. Materials: On huge words the newest letters develop through a soft luminance front rather than whole-word fades: a ramp ink -> mid grey -> pale over 4-5 letters (about 350 px at a 150 px cap height) runs across the line at 12-20 px/f, matching the camera pan, while new words still rise about a third of a line.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Letters`
- **Materials:** On huge words the newest letters develop through a soft luminance front rather than whole-word fades: a ramp ink -> mid grey -> pale over 4-5 letters (about 350 px at a 150 px cap height) runs across the line at 12-20 px/f, matching the camera pan, while new words still rise about a third of a line.
- **Timing:** 30 f for 11 letters; trailing letters 13 f with 1.5 f stagger.
- **Use when:** An "Introducing" over a photo; the end of a line entering at the frame edge.
- **Avoid when:** Body copy.

### Letters appear in random order

`dv-random-order-letters` · typography in motion · accent · energy calm · feature, walkthrough

The letters of a label or status line appear one by one in a shuffled order (each faint first, then full) until the word is whole.

- **Build:** <Letters mode="pop"> with onsets taken from a seeded permutation of the letter indices. Anatomy: Seeded permutation of letter onsets; each letter faint -> full in 2-4 f. Sound: Voice or none.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeFx.orderRanks`
- **Timing:** 24-32 f for a line (about one letter a frame) on an ease-in count.
- **Use when:** A button label appearing, an "Analyzing..." status line.
- **Avoid when:** Headlines.

### Letters swing up on an arc

`ty-letter-arc-swing` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, update, feature, sting, vertical · also `dv-letters-arc-swing`

Each letter shows small and turned, waiting up and to the right, and swings into place with a slight overshoot, one frame after the other: a quick ripple across the word.

- **Build:** <Letters text start mode="arc" />: 0.35x and 25 degrees about a centre below-right of the letter, M.letterArc over 5 f@30 (about 4 % over), 1 f apart; turn.{frames, ease} lands the turn after the scale.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Letters`
- **Timing:** About 0.4 s for a 7-letter word.
- **Use when:** A section title or a short label landing on a beat.
- **Avoid when:** Long words; more than one per act.

### Line opens room, then the key word types in

`dv-room-then-type` · typography in motion · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

A held line accelerates sideways to open room, then the key word types in letter by letter in the accent, and the line leaves with blur.

- **Build:** <LineSnap mode="room"> then <TypeOn kind="human"> in the opened slot; exit 'launch'. Anatomy: Pre-shift accelerating (-2 -> -36 px/f), typing about one letter a frame, exit left with blur. Sound: Voice.
- **Primitive:** `fx/LineSnap`, `fx/TypeOn`
- **Timing:** Pre-shift 20 f; typing 20 f; exit 12 f.
- **Use when:** The key word of a statement.
- **Avoid when:** Room moves slower than the typing.

### Multi-direction slam assembly

`ty-multi-direction-assemble` · typography in motion · accent · energy high · launch, sting, vertical

Each word of a short sentence flies in from a different side, oversized and streaked, and the sentence assembles on one baseline almost at once.

- **Build:** Lay out the final line and give each word a start offset from a different side (+-220 px in x, or +200 px in y) and a start scale of 1.4. Per word: p = prog(f, s + d_i, s + d_i + 20, E.out) with delays d = [0, 4, 10, 12, 16]; translate = offset x (1 - p) (vertical offsets through arrive), scale = lmix(1.4, 1, p), opacity 0 -> 1 over 5 f, so each word stays faint while it moves faster than 20 px/f and the blurred master streaks it along its own direction. One quiet piece may simply fade in over 8 f while the others fly; once the line is complete it drifts from scale 1 to 0.99 over 60 f.
- **Timing:** Per word 20 f E.out, 220 px travel (62, 47, 33, 23, 16 px/f on frames 1-5), scale 1.4 -> 1, opacity 5 f; delays 0/4/10/12/16 f; each word readable from about frame 5, the whole line resolved in about 36 f; then 1 -> 0.99 over 60 f.
- **Use when:** Re-spiking energy after a calm, read-paced card; a payoff line that needs a burst; 3-5 short words.
- **Avoid when:** Long words that would cross each other in flight; straight after another high-energy type move; calm films.

### Pre-centred words switch on every two frames

`dv-slot-pop-on-twos` · typography in motion · accent · energy high · launch, feature, sting, vertical

Words appear in one frame each, at full ink, in the slots of a line that is already laid out and centred, one every 2 frames (12 words a second); they can be erased in the same order.

- **Build:** <Words dur={1} rise={0} stagger={5}> (Words lays out the final centred line); erase with exit 'words' at 5 f; hit captions are HardStep on/off frames. Anatomy: Final layout solved first, words cut on in reading order, no fade, no scale; variants: huge left-aligned words (66 % of the frame width, 190 px tall) on the accent field; 10-frame steps for a slow caption; hit captions held 12-25 f and cut off in one frame. Sound: The completed phrase lands on a kick; hit captions sit on hits or in a stop-down silence.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** 5 f at 60 fps per word (2 f at 24-30 fps); erase 5 f apart in the same order; slow version 10 f per word; hit captions hold 30-60 f.
- **Use when:** A fast opener, a title that rides a camera move, hit captions over footage, huge words on a full accent field.
- **Avoid when:** Calm films; lines longer than 5 words (the build becomes a flicker).

### Sans line with a contrasting-voice payoff word

`dv-contrast-voice-pair` · typography in motion · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

A short phrase pairs a plain sans word with a payoff word in a contrasting voice (a handwritten script, a serif italic, small caps); the contrasting word enters 5-7 frames later.

- **Build:** <Words> with the payoff word in the second face and its own start. Anatomy: Sans word blur-fade-rise; contrasting word later; varied exits; a one-frame blank between phrases; variant: display caps fading in while a small italic connector types. Sound: A quiet breath before each cut.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Contrast by weight and size within the brand family (light vs heavy, or a mono payoff word). The full look relies on serif, italic; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** Entry 10-16 f; contrasting word +10-14 f; hold creeping 146 f.
- **Use when:** "No X." style lists; editorial films.
- **Avoid when:** Films whose brand has one family only.

### Scaled-echo extrusion

`ty-scaled-echo-extrusion` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, sting, feature

A hero title carries two or three faint copies scaled out behind it, a short depth extrusion that compresses as the title lands and then holds.

- **Build:** Stack k = 3, 2, 1 copies of the same text behind the title, with the title on top. Give copy k transform scale(1 + step x k) about a vanishing point, opacity 0.55, 0.35 and 0.2 for k = 1, 2, 3, and color mixColor(C.ink, stage colour, 0.5) (C.white mixed toward the stage on ink). Arrival: step = mix(0.03, 0.012, prog(f, land - 2, land + 20, E.out)), so the extrusion collapses inward as the title lands. Put the vanishing point on the text centre for a straight-on echo, or 0.3 W to one side or below it for a directional depth. Keep the hold alive by sliding the vanishing point about 40 px across the text over the hold, opposite to a 0.3 px/f line drift, so the echoes shift like real depth. Solid-block variant for a giant cropped word: 8-12 copies translated (k x 1 px, k x 1.5 px) behind the face, each a step darker (mixColor toward C.ink by k / 12), with no blur, bevel or shadow.
- **Timing:** Converge over 22 f on E.out (step 0.03 -> 0.012; outer copy edges stay under 7 px/f on a 500 px title). Copy opacity 0.55 / 0.35 / 0.2. Hold the whole card (36-60 f) with a vanishing-point slide of about 40 px on E.linear and a line drift of 0.3 px/f. The solid-block variant uses 8-12 one-pixel steps that do not animate relative to the face; the card still drifts at 0.3 px/f.
- **Use when:** A product name or a hero title of one to three words that needs weight in a flat sans. A giant cropped word that needs physical depth. A title card between two energetic acts.
- **Avoid when:** Body copy or lines over 3 words (the copies tangle inside the counters). Low-contrast stages, where the copies turn to haze. Blur, glow, bevels or drop shadows on the copies. A film that already uses the motion-trail echo of the word slams: pick one echo device.

### Set line resolves from blur left to right

`dv-focus-travel-line` · typography in motion · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

The whole line is laid out at once but only the first words are sharp; sharpness travels across it left to right, and the last word closes a gap as it sharpens.

- **Build:** <FocusWord mode="ui"> with the line split into words. Anatomy: Per-word blur and opacity by position; last word gap close. Sound: None. Materials: An address bar built from separate soft pills the colour of the canvas, defined only by a drop shadow (0 6px 18px at 8 %) and an inner top highlight (0 -2px 6px white at 90 %), with thin black line icons; no borders. As one line: `<TypeLine spec={{ preset: 'glide', text, at }}>` (the set line slides in 2.4 em and slows into a drift while its words resolve left to right, 3.5 f apart, solid in 8 f).
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypePresets.TypeLine`, `fx/FocusWord`
- **Materials:** An address bar built from separate soft pills the colour of the canvas, defined only by a drop shadow (0 6px 18px at 8 %) and an inner top highlight (0 -2px 6px white at 90 %), with thin black line icons; no borders.
- **Timing:** Sweep 34 f; gap close 16 f; continuous drift.
- **Use when:** A sentence that reads in one sweep; a calm opener.
- **Avoid when:** Lines the viewer has to wait for.

### Shared-letter morph

`ty-shared-letter-morph` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

One word turns into another: the letters both words share stay and slide into place while the new letters tumble in and click upright.

- **Build:** Split both words into glyph spans at measured, kerned positions; map shared characters (same letter, nearest index) so they keep their element and slide to the new x on prog(f, s, s + 24, E.out), while unshared old glyphs fade out over 6 f and the word spaces collapse over 8 f. Each new glyph starts at an offset of +-150 px in x and +-120 px in y from rand(`g${i}`) with a rotation of 90-180 degrees and animates to rest on E.out over 24 f, opacity 0 -> 1 over the first 12 f so it stays faint while faster than 20 px/f, with start times spread over 56 f and the last glyph dropping from above. Check every frame on a contact sheet so no in-between state spells another word.
- **Timing:** Space collapse 8 f; old glyph fade 6 f; each new glyph 24 f E.out (about 45 px/f on frame 1), opacity 12 f; starts spread over 56 f; hold at least 36 f after the last glyph settles.
- **Use when:** Two words that share letters and whose relationship is the point (before and after, problem and product); one memorable word turn per film.
- **Avoid when:** Fewer than 2 shared letters; words longer than about 8 letters; fast films where 60 f of letter flight is too slow.

### Slice glitch into a speed streak

`ty-slice-glitch-streak` · typography in motion · accent · energy high · launch, sting, feature

A word jolts into sideways-displaced horizontal slices for two frames, then stretches into a solid capsule that races off as a streak, and the next word lands in its wake.

- **Build:** Slice: for 2 f decided with fd, render the word as 6-8 stacked copies, each clipped to one horizontal band with clip-path: inset(), and offset each band by sign x 0.08-0.25 em, both drawn from rand(`${b}:${fd(f)}`). Under 30% of the bands, lay a C.mute copy offset 0.03 em (one hue, no RGB fringes), and raise the variable 'wght' by 100 for those two frames; frame 3 renders clean. Smear: from s, scaleX = mix(1, 1.8, prog(f, s, s + 18, E.contact)) about the word's left edge, so the right edge accelerates to about 70 px/f on the last frame (render the blurred master). Over those last 10 f, fade the text out while a capsule (C.ink on paper or C.white on ink, radius 50%) fades in over the same box and its height shrinks from the cap height to 0.35 of it. Streak: the capsule keeps its handoff speed, with head x = x_e + v_e x (f - e) and a trailing tail of length clamp(v x 1.5, 0, 240) px, until it clears the frame edge. Next word: it enters in the wake, layered under the streak, with translateX -320 -> 0 on p = prog(f, e + 4, e + 28, E.outSoft), opacity 0 -> 1 over 8 f and blurIn(p, 16), so it is faint while fast and readable once it drops under 20 px/f. The 2 f slice alone, with no smear, works as a hit on privacy or obfuscation copy.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Make the streak a flat solid capsule in C.ink or C.white with a speed-scaled tail and true motion blur. No bloom on the type or the streak, the trail keeps the capsule's one tone, and the glitch copies stay in C.mute. The full look relies on glow, purple; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Slice: 2 f via fd, clean on frame 3. Smear: 18 f on E.contact, scaleX 1 -> 1.8; for a word up to 450 px wide the right edge ends near 70 px/f. Text-to-capsule crossfade over the last 10 f. The streak cruises at that speed and clears a 1920 frame in about 15 f, with a tail of at most 240 px. Next word: 320 px over 24 f on E.outSoft from e + 4 (58 px/f on frame 1, under 20 px/f from frame 7), opacity over 8 f. Hold it at least 54 f.
- **Use when:** A speed or performance claim, where the word itself turns into motion. Handing a name off to a thread, packet or line that carries into the next scene. The 2 f slice alone on 'private', 'encrypted' or 'blocked'.
- **Avoid when:** Calm films. More than once per film. Words wider than about 450 px at the smear, where the edge would pass 80 px/f. Long lines. Coloured fringes or a tint shift along the trail.

### Slice-band glyph assembly

`ty-slice-band-assembly` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, sting, feature

Each letter builds up from thin horizontal slices that slide in from slightly different offsets at slightly different moments, faint and pale at first, until the word locks solid.

- **Build:** Measure the word with measureTracked. Give each glyph an inline-grid cell holding N = 5 stacked copies of itself (6 copies for type above 160 px), with all copies in grid-area 1/1. Clip copy b to its band with clip-path: inset(calc(b * 100% / N - 0.5px) -0.1em calc((N - 1 - b) * 100% / N - 0.5px) -0.1em), on a line box padded 0.12 em on top and 0.26 em below, so neighbouring bands overlap by 1 px and no descender or overhang gets shaved. Band (i, b) starts at s + d, with d = fd(12 x rand(`${i}:${b}`)) (add 1 f per glyph for a left-to-right bias), and runs on p = prog(f, s + d, s + d + 20, E.out): translateX (1 - p) x sx x 0.12 em, where sx = rand(`x${i}:${b}`) > 0.5 ? 1 : -1; translateY (1 - arrive(p)) x 0.04 em; opacity over its first 8 f on E.linear; and color mixColor(C.mute, C.ink, p) on paper (stage tint to C.white on ink). On the frame the last band lands, swap the band stacks for one intact text layer, decided with fd, so no seam survives antialiasing, then tighten the tracking 0.03 em -> the token over 44 f on E.out. Beside a mark that slides aside, start the build at the slide's peak-velocity frame, so the letters seem to be pulled out by its motion.
- **Timing:** Each band takes 20 f on E.out, with opacity over 8 f on E.linear and colour over the same 20 f. Band delays are 0-12 f from rand (plus 1 f per glyph if biased). The whole word is built in about 32 f (about 40 f with the bias). Offsets are 0.12 em sideways and 0.04 em vertical: about 4 px/f on frame 1 at 120 px type, so no blur. The swap to intact text takes 1 f, then the tracking tightens over 44 f on E.out. Hold at least 60 f with a drift of 0.3 px/f.
- **Use when:** A product or feature name that should feel assembled or digital. A name set beside a modular or pixel mark, including the one end-lockup build when the film bookends with it. A short title after a quiet beat.
- **Avoid when:** Lines over about 3 words, or type under 48 px (bands thinner than 3 px alias into noise). Prose. Delay spreads wide enough that the half-built word reads as broken for more than about 30 f. A film that already has a scramble decode.

### Taglines swap on the second with a small pop

`dv-tagline-metronome` · typography in motion · accent · energy calm · launch, vertical

Small taglines replace each other exactly every second; the new one appears slightly small and pops to size in 2 frames while its contrast rises.

- **Build:** HardStep swaps every 60 f; scale via a 2 f tween; opacity contrast over 20 f. Anatomy: Hard swap; scale 0.88 -> 1 in 2 f; contrast up over 16-28 f. Sound: On round seconds, not on beats.
- **Primitive:** `fx/HardStep`
- **Timing:** Every 60 f; pop 2 f.
- **Use when:** A run of short claims over a photo.
- **Avoid when:** More than about four swaps.

### Ticker words slam in, old words cut off the edge

`dv-ticker-slam` · typography in motion · accent · energy high · launch, sting

Each new word enters from the right with a huge first-frame jump (135-290 px) and an expo tail; the older words are pushed left and cut off by the frame.

- **Build:** <Chain recentre="jump" ink="pop" edgeMask={{ left: 0 }}> with the line anchored right. Anatomy: Jump frame + tail per word, the line shifts by the new word's width; exits on single frames at the left edge. Sound: A hit per word.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Chain`
- **Timing:** 2 f jump + 12 f tail per word.
- **Use when:** A rapid list of verbs or features on hits.
- **Avoid when:** Copy that must be read in full.

### Title decodes from its centre

`ty-scramble-decode` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, sting, loop · also `dv-centre-out-decode`

A title opens outward from its middle behind two fronts of flat accent blocks; or glyphs of each letter's own class cycle ten times a second and lock outward from the centre.

- **Build:** <Scramble text title edge="mosaic" start /> opens the title in 3 f@60 a glyph (an 11-glyph title in about half a second), a 0.55 em band of accent blocks on each front, no glow. Scramble form: rateHz 10, order 'centre', steps for an anagram of the title's own letters. The decode span is declared stepped.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Scramble`
- **Conditions:** light built into the device (core, body, falloff), never a uniform halo
- **Timing:** 0.4-0.6 s for a title; hold 1 s after.
- **Use when:** A product or film title, once; a version number in an update film.
- **Avoid when:** Running copy; more than once per film.

### Typewriter on an ease-out progress

`dv-typing-ease-progress` · typography in motion · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

A line types at full opacity, character-quantised but on an ease-out: 41 % of its width after one frame, 66 % after two, then slowing; contrasting accent words type in the same pass.

- **Build:** <TypeOn kind="stream" ease={E.snapOut}>. Anatomy: Character count follows an ease-out; accent words in a contrasting face inline. Sound: Voice.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeOn`
- **Timing:** 54 f at 60 fps.
- **Use when:** A line that should feel written in one stroke.
- **Avoid when:** Prompts (people do not type on an ease).

### Typing whose newest characters arrive smeared

`dv-typing-smear-lead` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

Text types fast while its newest 2-30 characters arrive as a horizontal smear (or a soft accent ghost running ahead of the white text) that sharpens behind the caret: speed you can see.

- **Build:** TypeOn kind 'stream' or 'prompt' plus a smear window: draw the last n characters a second time through a fixed horizontal-blur copy (the trail prop gives the colour half of it). Anatomy: Committed text sharp; a trailing window of the last 2-3 characters (or a 10-30 character ghost in the accent ahead of the text) with horizontal blur; typing in bursts. Sound: Keypress ticks only when the typing is slow enough to hear; a fast run takes none.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeOn.TypeOn`
- **Timing:** 60-130 characters a second (1 char a frame at 60 fps); each character sharpens over 6 f; bursts over 22-34 f.
- **Use when:** A prompt or URL typed fast into the product, especially just before a cut hides the end of the sentence.
- **Avoid when:** Slow, readable typing (the smear then looks like a rendering fault).

### Word cuts on and drifts, then leaves the same way

`dv-cut-on-drift` · typography in motion · accent · energy calm · any

Labels appear in one frame at full ink and keep drifting (diagonally apart, or sideways on an expo-out), hold briefly and accelerate out along the same line.

- **Build:** <Words dur={1} rise={0}> inside a drift transform; exit 'launch' along the drift. Anatomy: Cut-on (1 f fade), drift 60-70 px, short hold, launch exit. Sound: Each label near a beat.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`
- **Timing:** Drift 26-68 f; hold 8 f; exit 16 f accelerating (2, 4, 8, 14 px...).
- **Use when:** Two labels that relate (a pair of words apart in the frame); a single word between scenes.
- **Avoid when:** Text that must sit still to be read.

### Word decodes from a low-res pixel version

`dv-resolution-ladder-decode` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, sting

A word appears as a coarse low-resolution pixel version in the accent, then half-resolved in a pale tone, then crisp in the ink, one frame each, and settles with a small posterised overshoot.

- **Build:** <Pixelate> in-phase only on the word with a three-size ladder (pixelLadder of 3 sizes) and the colour stepped per state. Anatomy: Three resolution states, colour accent -> pale -> ink; a stepped spring settle. Sound: A drum on the decode, a kick on the settle.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Pixel.Pixelate`
- **Timing:** Decode 7 f (one state per 2-3 f at 60 fps); settle 7 f on twos.
- **Use when:** Words in a film about images, rendering or AI generation.
- **Avoid when:** Small type (the low-res stage is unreadable mush below about 60 px).

### Word flips up from a flat line

`dv-flip-up-word` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

A word flips up about its baseline from a flat line (rotateX) while rising and darkening.

- **Build:** Recipe: rotateX(90deg -> 0) about the baseline with perspective 800 px plus the Words rise. Anatomy: Glyph height 12 -> 57 px in 3 frames, rise 66 px, grey to ink. Sound: None.
- **Timing:** Height 8 f, position 25 f, colour 20 f.
- **Use when:** A word that should feel lifted off the page.
- **Avoid when:** Thin type (the flat phase disappears).

### Word halves slide out from behind a plate

`dv-split-word-emerge` · typography in motion · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

The two halves of one word emerge from under a plate (masked by it) and drift outward, the word opening around the object.

- **Build:** Recipe: two Words spans inside a clip-path that excludes the plate, translated outward on E.snapOut. Anatomy: Two halves clipped by the plate's edge, drifting apart. Sound: None.
- **Timing:** 40 f ease-out.
- **Use when:** A word that wraps a product or a dock.
- **Avoid when:** Words that split badly.

### Word inks along a colour path

`dv-hue-path-ink` · typography in motion · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

Each new word appears at full size but pale and walks along a colour path into the ink, letter by letter from one end; the colour change is the reveal.

- **Build:** <HueSweep> house one-hue path (9 f per word at 30 fps, words 10-12 f apart). Recipe: background-image a ten-stop gradient, background-size 300 % 100 %, background-clip text, background-position-x 100 -> 0 % over 48 f. Anatomy: Lightness held first, then darkened through the accent into the ink; the front crosses the word with the right end leading (or right to left for a cooling ramp); variant: the first word nudges 18 px into centre while it colours. Sound: A soft whoosh on the first word; word cadence off the beat. Materials: A wide spectral band slides right to left through the label and leaves ink behind: the line arrives as a horizontal rainbow (yellow, orange, magenta, red, olive), the band (about three times the label's width) slides left on a bezier (0.37, 0.13, 0.26, 0.95) at about 12 px/f, so mid-move the line reads warm at its end and cool at its start, and the tail of the band is ink. Ten stops from warm to green, teal, blue, navy and ink.
- **Primitive:** `fx/HueSweep`
- **Materials:** A wide spectral band slides right to left through the label and leaves ink behind: the line arrives as a horizontal rainbow (yellow, orange, magenta, red, olive), the band (about three times the label's width) slides left on a bezier (0.37, 0.13, 0.26, 0.95) at about 12 px/f, so mid-move the line reads warm at its end and cool at its start, and the tail of the band is ink. Ten stops from warm to green, teal, blue, navy and ink.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform; the film's one spectral accent
- **Timing:** 18-20 f per word, onsets 20-24 f apart; a ramp front of 13 f with a 30 f tail; AI lines 28-44 f each.
- **Use when:** A text-led opener, an AI line that should feel generated, a keyword.
- **Avoid when:** More than one per act; a full rainbow walk (it reads as a template).

### Words rise and drop onto one baseline with overshoot

`dv-baseline-converge-overshoot` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

One word rises from below and the next drops from above onto a shared baseline, each landing with a real overshoot, while the background pans with a pulse.

- **Build:** Recipe: per word a damped spring on y (SPR.landing) from ±0.8 em. Anatomy: Alternate directions; landing overshoot 11-19 %, zeta 0.46-0.57; a 2-step rise. Sound: A kick on the first landing, onsets per word.
- **Timing:** Landings 12-22 f; pan 72 f.
- **Use when:** A playful two-word title on a coloured field.
- **Avoid when:** A film that already spends its one spring elsewhere.

### Anagrams reshuffle and lock

`dv-anagram-converge` · typography in motion · signature · energy medium · launch, sting

Two jumbled words sit apart and every 2-3 frames their letters reshuffle (real anagrams of the target words) while they converge and lock; or one word becomes another by swapping letters one at a time.

- **Build:** <Scramble steps> (anagram stages); letter swap with Scramble order 'ltr' and steps of one letter. Anatomy: Letters re-ordered in steps, colour shifting each step; convergence on the last step; letter-swap variant: letters drop or rise a few px as they change. Sound: Ticks on the steps.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Scramble`
- **Timing:** Steps every 4-6 f at 60 fps; 34 f; letter swap about 2 f per letter.
- **Use when:** A name or a claim that is "made" in front of the viewer.
- **Avoid when:** Long words (beyond about 8 letters it reads as noise).

### Caption resolves out of a light streak

`dv-streak-resolve` · typography in motion · signature · energy medium · launch, sting, vertical

The next caption first exists as a thin bright horizontal streak (letters unreadable), widens, turns into a heavily smeared word, then snaps sharp: the caption is born from light rather than faded in. The exit is the same device reversed: the caption dims, gains a horizontal ghost and collapses into a wide bright streak (or a thin grey line) that vanishes.

- **Build:** Build: <StreakResolve at text x y font light> (fx/Streak): the caption through a heavy sideways blur squeezed to a hairline with a bright core, opening over the first half of 15 f on E.whipBuild (width 0.89 -> 1.03 of the caption, height to the line: measured), then the word smeared sideways for 5 f, then sharp, one sample a frame; exit={{ at }} dims to 40 %, ghosts, and collapses into a widening streak on twos (18 f). Anatomy: Stage 1 streak (a 1-4 px tall bar, 200-660 px wide, front-loaded widening), stage 2 a horizontally smeared word for 2 f, stage 3 sharp. Variant: the smear grows rightward out of the previous word on twos, then a 2-frame scramble, then sharp. Exit: dim to 40 %, ghost, collapse to a 330-600 px streak on twos, accelerating. Sound: No hit of its own; it rides the voice onset. Materials: Relay construction: the outgoing caption gets a trailing ghost (4 f), blurs sideways into a doubled bar (4 f), becomes a bright horizontal streak about 1100 px wide with a fainter offset copy (+40, +12 px at 35 %) for 6 f, breaks for one frame into blocky glyph fragments (a decode) and lands sharp as the next caption; on twos except the decode frame.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Streak.StreakResolve`
- **Materials:** Relay construction: the outgoing caption gets a trailing ghost (4 f), blurs sideways into a doubled bar (4 f), becomes a bright horizontal streak about 1100 px wide with a fainter offset copy (+40, +12 px at 35 %) for 6 f, breaks for one frame into blocky glyph fragments (a decode) and lands sharp as the next caption; on twos except the decode frame.
- **Timing:** Streak 3-15 f, smear 5 f, sharp: 8-20 f in all, stepped, front-loaded; the caption leads the spoken word by 2-16 f.
- **Use when:** Voice-led films where captions follow the narration; the first caption after a section break; a word that grows out of the one before it.
- **Avoid when:** Long lines; anything that must be read on its first frames.

### Masked roll swap with a pre-zoom

`dv-roll-swap-bracket` · typography in motion · signature · energy high · launch, feature, sting

A word inside a bracket rolls up out of the mask while the next word rolls in from below (vertical blur on the roll), after a small anticipation zoom; the bracket grows to the new width.

- **Build:** MaskRise for the incoming word, an upward launch exit for the outgoing one inside one clip; the bracket width via a 14 f tween; SnapZoom pre with a 4 % build. Anatomy: Pre-zoom (anticipation), roll up/out and up/in, box 175 -> 327 px, cubic-out settle. Sound: A key or kick on the roll.
- **Primitive:** `fx/MaskRise`
- **Timing:** Pre-zoom 8 f; roll 10 f; settle 14 f.
- **Use when:** Swapping the key noun of a held line on a beat.
- **Avoid when:** Swaps faster than every 1.5 s.

### Old word erodes while new letters rise

`dv-erode-and-rise` · typography in motion · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

The old word disappears from its end, letter by letter, each blurring out horizontally, while the new word's letters rise into place behind it.

- **Build:** Recipe: Letters build for the incoming word plus a per-letter exit (opacity and a horizontal ladder blur copy) in reverse order. Anatomy: Exit letters right to left, 1-2 f each with a horizontal smear; entry letters 3 f stagger, expo-out, full opacity in 3 f. Sound: Voice.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeFx.ErodeRise`
- **Timing:** 40 f in all; new letters 20 f each.
- **Use when:** Swapping one key word in a held line.
- **Avoid when:** Words the viewer has not read yet.

### One-word slam sequence

`ty-kinetic-word-slams` · typography in motion · signature · energy high · launch, sting, vertical

A line is read one huge word at a time: each word hits oversized and blurred, settles, then is sucked away as the next word cuts in.

- **Build:** Each word is its own card, fitted to about 77% of the frame width with fitSize. Entry: scale = lmix(1.35, 1, p), p = prog(f, cue - 1, cue + 21, E.outSoft), opacity 0 -> 1 over 3 f, blur = blurIn(p, 12), then a 6 f drift (scale x 1.01). Never start above 1.35x: a larger start leaves the outer letters of a frame-wide word moving faster than 20 px/f after the blur has cleared. Exit: scale x lmix(1, 0.6, q), q = prog(f, end - 14, end, E.in), opacity to 0 on E.smooth over the same window, then a hard cut to the next word on its slam's first frame, with every cut on an act boundary so the blurred master never smears two words together. Optional echo: two copies behind the word use the entry progress at f - 2 and f - 4, at 0.35 and 0.18 opacity, tinted 50% toward the ground, so they converge into the word by +12 f.
- **Timing:** Entry 22 f E.outSoft from 1.35x (the edges of a 1120 px word start at about 43 px/f, faded and blurred, and are near 22 px/f by frame 4 when the blur clears), blur 12 -> 0 by about frame 4, drift 6 f, exit 14 f E.in to 0.6x (last frame about 72 px/f, nearly transparent); 36-42 f per word (0.6-0.7 s), last word held at least 54 f under a 1-2% scale creep; every hit on a beat.
- **Use when:** A punchy 3-5 word line on a strong beat; a problem statement or rhythmic claim; vertical formats where one word fills the screen.
- **Avoid when:** More than one sequence per film; lines over 5 words; calm films; a card for a lone connector word (fold it into the next word).

### Oversize word slide-in

`ty-oversize-blur-slide-in` · typography in motion · signature · energy high · launch, sting, feature

A huge word arrives streaked from beside the frame and brakes on a long tail, and a trailing word follows from further out and closes the gap so the phrase locks together.

- **Build:** Type height 21-25% of the frame. Word 1: x = x_f + 0.4W x (1 - prog(f, s, s + 90, E.out)) - 0.5 x (f - s), a long braking tail on top of a slow drift that never stops, with opacity 0.2 -> 1 over the 16 f it takes to fall below 20 px/f, so it travels faded. Word 2 starts 16 f later with a larger offset (0.6W) on the same curve, so the gap between the words shrinks from about 1.7x to 1x over about 80 f, and its opacity rises 0.2 -> 1 over 68 f; letters may fade on left to right 2 f apart as each word slows. Frame 1 runs about 52 px/f (78 for word 2), so render the blurred master; blurIn(p, 10) stands in for the sharp preview.
- **Timing:** Brake 90 f E.out (feels like a 33 f time constant); word 1 offset 0.4W (768 px), word 2 0.6W from +16 f; drift 0.5 px/f; opacity from 0.2, readable below 20 px/f from frame 16 (word 2 from frame 21); gap 1.7x -> 1x over 80 f.
- **Use when:** The energy peak of a type act; a two-word claim; a cold open whose first frame already moves.
- **Avoid when:** Long phrases; when screen direction must run the other way across the cut; small type.

### Oversized landing with a sweeping cool

`ty-oversized-landing` · typography in motion · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, vertical · also `dv-oversize-landing`

The payoff word cuts in larger than its rest size and settles down to it, never below, while the accent cools to ink behind a soft front that crosses the word.

- **Build:** <Oversize start={f} from={1.6} dur={36 f@60} accent={C.accent} ink={C.ink} cool="sweep" coolEase={E.glideOut} sweep={{ width: 0.8 }}> around the word (text inside uses currentColor). The settle runs on M.oversize on a composited layer; origin 'center' for a centred title, 'left center' for a left-aligned line. A first word may also start defocused and snap sharp exactly when the second word lands (defocus, defocusUntil: a declared step). In a chain use oversizeFirst; in a fragment Words oversize={{ from, dur }}. As one line: `<TypeLine spec={{ preset: 'land', text, at, lead, scaleFrom }}>` (x1.7 on E.glideOut over 34 f, a slight defocus riding the scale, a given accent home 12 f early; with `lead` the other words append 12 f apart while the line re-centres).
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypePresets.TypeLine`, `fx/Oversize`
- **Materials:** The landed word cools from a hot accent to ink as a sweep: a band about 30 % of the word wide (hot -> a dark shade -> ink) crosses left to right in 40 f, expo-out, while the word shrinks, so the first letters are ink while the last are still hot.
- **Timing:** From x1.28-1.9 (house 1.6; up to about x2.7 with a defocused start), settle 22-56 f@60 (house 36), colour home about 12 f@60 before the scale.
- **Use when:** The payoff word, a first word, a product name: one per act.
- **Avoid when:** Long lines (the oversized frame crops them); several oversized landings in a row (the device wears out).

### Quiet type swells on the drop

`ty-swell-on-drop` · typography in motion · signature · energy high · launch, sting, vertical

A word appears small and low-contrast and waits through the build, then swells to hero size, with 90% of the growth landing exactly on the beat drop.

- **Build:** Set the word at about 9% of the frame height, centred, in C.mute (or at 0.5 opacity on ink), and bring it in quietly: per-letter opacity pops 5-6 f apart decided with fd, or ty-typeon-timeboxed. Put the drop frame h on the music's downbeat, register it in src/sync.ts, and scale the group about its centre with k = lmix(1, 2.5, prog(f, h - 32, h + 22, E.glide)), so 90% of the log-scale growth lands on h and the rest settles over 22 f. Run color mixColor(C.mute, C.ink, prog(f, h - 32, h, E.smooth)) so size and contrast peak together. Drive the scale with transform, never font-size, and keep the starting width under about 420 px, so the outer edges peak near 17 px/f (21 px/f at 2.9x) and the word stays readable through the swell; render the blurred master for the frames above 12 px/f. After the settle, keep it alive with a 0.3 px/f drift or a cam-living-hold creep, or cut within 54 f.
- **Timing:** Letters 5-6 f apart at 9% of the frame height. Swell over 54 f on E.glide, starting at h - 32 so 90% lands on h: scale 1 -> 2.5 (2.9 at most) in log space, with the outer edges of a 420 px word peaking at about 16.5 px/f around frame 17. Contrast goes C.mute -> ink over the 32 f before h. Hold at most 54 f after h, or 90-120 f if this is the final lockup's one appearance.
- **Use when:** A hero word or product name that should detonate on the drop after a quiet intro. The one appearance of the final wordmark when the music builds into the end. A single-word answer after a question beat.
- **Avoid when:** There is no real musical hit to land on. Words wide enough to swell past the safe area. Using it more than once per film. Stacking a separate scale punch or camera kick on the same hit.

### Scattered letters assemble into the word

`dv-letters-scatter-assemble` · typography in motion · signature · energy medium · launch, sting

The letters of the payoff word start scattered (random offsets above and below, grey, almost still), accelerate gently and snap into the word together, usually during a camera push.

- **Build:** Recipe: Letters positions from prefix widths, each offset by a seeded vector that decays on an ease-in. Anatomy: Per letter a seeded offset (up to 330 px), slow float, then an ease-in convergence with a hard landing; grey to ink on arrival. Sound: Voice; or a soft lock on the landing.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeFx.ScatterAssemble`
- **Timing:** 34-60 f; float 40 f, final convergence 13 f; each glyph expo-out when it lands.
- **Use when:** The payoff word of an act; a word in a mono or brand face.
- **Avoid when:** Fast films (the drift needs a beat to read).

### Typeface cycles while the line steps larger

`dv-typeface-cycle` · typography in motion · signature · energy high · launch, sting

Every 3 frames the typeface of a title swaps (serif, mono, light grotesk, heavy), while the line steps larger; it lands on the brand face.

- **Build:** Recipe: an array of font stacks indexed by a stepped frame inside <Stepped fps={8}>, measured under FontGate so each swap re-centres. Anatomy: Hard swaps of the face, the line re-centred each swap, scale stepping up. Sound: None needed; or a tick per swap. Materials: Only the brand word shuffles through font styles every 4-6 f (regular, black, thin extended, black extended, back to regular) while the rest of the line stays still; cap height constant, the extended styles pushing the word about 25 % wider. With a variable font this is a wght and wdth change per state; the house bans italic, so leave the slant axis out.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Cycle between weights and widths of the brand family only. The full look relies on serif; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeFx.FontCycle`
- **Materials:** Only the brand word shuffles through font styles every 4-6 f (regular, black, thin extended, black extended, back to regular) while the rest of the line stays still; cap height constant, the extended styles pushing the word about 25 % wider. With a variable font this is a wght and wdth change per state; the house bans italic, so leave the slant axis out.
- **Timing:** 8 swaps a second (every 7-8 f); 38 f in all.
- **Use when:** A launch about type, image or style; a title once.
- **Avoid when:** Any film whose brand face must be respected from the first frame.

### Word shown first as a block of its own size

`dv-word-block-placeholder` · typography in motion · signature · energy high · launch, feature, vertical

Each word first appears as a solid colour block exactly its size, then becomes the word, which drops 25 px onto the baseline; blocks can rotate through the accents' tints.

- **Build:** BlockStep silhouette per word (the incoming element's flat silhouette steps to the real word), or HardStep on/off frames with a rect of the measured word box. Anatomy: Block (the word's box, one colour, 3 f) -> word; alternate words rise or drop; 1-2 words per step. Sound: Voice words; a ding on the line's completion.
- **Primitive:** `fx/BlockStep`
- **Timing:** 4 f per word at 60 fps; block 6 f; 4-5 f per word in a run.
- **Use when:** A voice-led headline in a bold, graphic film.
- **Avoid when:** Calm films; more than one line.

### Words fly in from behind the camera

`dv-fly-past-lens-word` · typography in motion · signature · energy high · launch, sting

Each word starts about 10x its size (one letter fills the frame), blurred and off-centre, and shrinks into its slot: the words seem to come from behind the viewer.

- **Build:** <Oversize from={10} dur={23} defocus={14} defocusDur={18}> per word with an x offset that converges; stagger 10. Anatomy: Per word: scale 10x to 1, a lateral start (left, centre, right in turn), blur clearing as it shrinks; staggered. Sound: The first word on a kick (+19 ms); a soft air pass per word. As one line: `<TypeLine spec={{ preset: 'fly', text, at }}>` (each word from x5 and soft, landing in 14 f in log scale on E.snapOut, 10 f apart, touching; the spaces open after the last lands).
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypePresets.TypeLine`, `fx/Oversize`
- **Timing:** About 23 f per word, stagger 10 f, sharp by the last word's landing.
- **Use when:** A tagline or a closing line on a strong beat; once per film.
- **Avoid when:** Calm films; more than 4 words.

### Words jump through positions, leaving fading stamps

`dv-jump-echo-stamp` · typography in motion · signature · energy high · launch, sting, vertical

Words teleport on ones through about five converging positions on their way to the final line; every visited position leaves a stamp of the word that fades out, with corner ticks riding along.

- **Build:** Build: <EchoStamp at x y from={{ x: 640, y: -250 }} ticks={{ color }}>{word}</EchoStamp> (fx/Echoes): on ones at 30 fps through progress 0, .40, .60, .66, .75, hold, 1 (12 f at 60); each left position leaves a stamp from 75 % that fades in 10 f; the hold leaves none; two L ticks ride the live word. Anatomy: Positions on a converging path (progress 0, .40, .60, .66, .75, hold, 1); each stamp a copy at that position fading 0.2 per frame. Sound: An impact on the landing.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Echoes.EchoStamp`
- **Timing:** 12 f at 60 fps for the jumps; stamps fade over 10 f; first jump 227-292 px.
- **Use when:** A hook line that should feel like a camera-less glitch of motion; a title in a techno film.
- **Avoid when:** Calm films; more than once.

### Answer streams and its card grows line by line

`dv-stream-card-grow` · ui choreography · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

A reply streams in 5-6 characters a frame, line by line, and its card grows a line at a time to hold it; several text blocks of one card can stream at once.

- **Build:** <TypeOn kind="stream"> inside a container whose height is snapBox() of the line count (HardStep) or an E.snapOut tween per line. Anatomy: Stream text; the container height snaps (or eases 6-10 f) per new line; variant: headline, outline and body blocks stream simultaneously with live re-wrapping. Sound: None per line; one soft pop when the card completes. Materials: A tiny caret blinks, becomes an empty outlined pill (1 px white at 50 %, about 70 px placeholder), then a small caps label types into it (about 1 character a frame at 60) while the pill snaps wider with every character, no ease.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeOn`, `fx/HardStep`
- **Materials:** A tiny caret blinks, becomes an empty outlined pill (1 px white at 50 %, about 70 px placeholder), then a small caps label types into it (about 1 character a frame at 60) while the pill snaps wider with every character, no ease.
- **Timing:** 60-150 characters a second; card fills in 29-50 f.
- **Use when:** Showing an AI answer or a generated document.
- **Avoid when:** Text the viewer must read in full.

### Field fills a word at a time, each word lit for one frame

`dv-field-word-flash` · ui choreography · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

A query field fills one whole word every 2 frames, each new word in the accent for exactly one frame; a prompt card can fill one line per frame.

- **Build:** <TypeOn kind="field" accent>. Anatomy: Words cut on whole; one-frame accent flash per word; variant: a 3-line prompt in 3 frames. Sound: Typing ticks or a bubble pop when the card completes.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeOn`
- **Timing:** 12 words a second (one every 5 f at 60 fps); a line per frame for a prompt card.
- **Use when:** Showing that the product understands a request instantly; a montage of prompts.
- **Avoid when:** Text the viewer must read word by word.

### Words added into a pill that resizes instantly

`dv-pill-resizes-per-word` · ui choreography · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

Words appear one at a time inside a pill and the pill takes its new width in one frame each time, with uneven gaps that feel like thinking.

- **Build:** <HardStep> snapBox of the measured text widths; words pop. Anatomy: Pill width = snapBox of the text width; words cut on. Sound: None, or a soft tick per word.
- **Primitive:** `fx/HardStep`
- **Timing:** Word gaps 15, 33, 8 f (uneven).
- **Use when:** A prompt or idea being formed; a chip that grows.
- **Avoid when:** Eased container growth next to it (keep it hard).

### Prompt typing that slows on its last word

`dv-typing-prompt-decel` · product demo · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

A prompt types at a steady rate and slows on its last word, letter by letter, so the request lands with intent.

- **Build:** <TypeOn kind="prompt"> (last word x1.6 house; raise to x2.5 for emphasis). Anatomy: Steady about 30-33 characters a second, then one character every 4-8 f on the last word. Sound: Typing ticks, the last key softer. Materials: When the text outgrows the field it scrolls left under a feathered left edge (a 50-70 px mask) instead of a hard clip; once typing stops the caret blinks slowly (12 f on, 20 f off).
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeOn`
- **Materials:** When the text outgrows the field it scrolls left under a feathered left edge (a 50-70 px mask) instead of a hard clip; once typing stops the caret blinks slowly (12 f on, 20 f off).
- **Timing:** Whole prompt 50-90 f; last word 1.6-3x slower.
- **Use when:** The question that triggers the product's answer.
- **Avoid when:** Typing that is cut before it ends.

### Typing by a person, with word-end pauses

`dv-typing-human` · product demo · workhorse · energy calm · any

Text types the way a person types: runs inside words, a pause of 1-2 frames at word ends, an I-beam caret; the UI around it reacts (a send button pops before the sentence ends, icons pop when it is done).

- **Build:** <TypeOn kind="human">; a send button pop is press/springBox started 4-6 f before the last key.
