Anatomy: Characters cut on (optionally a 4 f fade each); variants: a line typing above the previous one so the stack builds upward; a first word that pops whole and a second that types; a wrap onto a second line. Sound: Key clicks per keystroke at -13 to -24 dBFS, or none.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeOn`
- **Timing:** 24-45 characters a second inside words, +2-4 f per space; human kind: 30 cps in runs, one key pause at commas.
- **Use when:** A prompt or search typed into the product, a title on a device screen, any line that should feel human.
- **Avoid when:** Machine output (use a stream); long paragraphs.

### Typing that starts mostly done after a cut

`dv-typing-elided` · product demo · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough, vertical

After a cut, the prompt is already 50-80 % typed and the rest types with deceleration: the film skips the boring part.

- **Build:** <TypeOn from={0.65} kind="stream" ease={E.type}>. Anatomy: First frame 50-80 % typed; the rest decelerates. Sound: A keypress bed rather than per-key clicks.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeOn`
- **Timing:** About 93 cps for 5 f, then 59, 51... slowing; 75 f for 51 characters.
- **Use when:** Several prompts in a row, montages of requests.
- **Avoid when:** The first prompt of a film (show one typed in full first).

### Placeholder deletes, the real value types in bursts

`dv-typing-backspace-retype` · product demo · accent · energy calm · feature, walkthrough

A placeholder in a field deletes quickly, then the real value types in irregular 1-2 character bursts: the field is being edited, not filled.

- **Build:** Two TypeOn runs: the first with its count reversed (characters shown = n - count), the second human kind. Anatomy: Backspace run (about 11 characters in 10 f), a beat, then bursts. Sound: A chat pop mid-typing if a reply comes in.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeOn`
- **Timing:** Delete about 33 characters a second; retype about 26 a second in bursts; 48 f in all.
- **Use when:** A URL, a name or a setting being changed in the product.
- **Avoid when:** Fields the viewer has not seen filled before.

### Typing that accelerates into a whip

`dv-typing-accelerate-whip` · product demo · accent · energy high · launch, feature, walkthrough

The gaps between keys shrink (5, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1 frames) while the camera follows the caret on a decaying push, then whips away before the line ends.

- **Build:** <TypeOn kind="prompt" gaps={ACCEL.typing} skip> with typeOn() caret camera into whip(). Anatomy: Accelerating key gaps; camera tracks the caret (decay power 2.6) in close-up; the whip hides the last keys. Sound: One click per keystroke; the music drops out for 0.3 s before the next hit.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeOn`
- **Timing:** Gaps 5, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1 f at 60 fps (20 f in all); close-up runs 12, 12, 7, 5, 7, 5, 5, 5 f per character.
- **Use when:** Handing off from a typed request to the product's reaction.
- **Avoid when:** A line the viewer must read to the end.

### Accent on the newest arrival

`cl-accent-on-newest` · colour and light · workhorse · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch, vertical · also `dv-transient-accent-word`

Whatever just landed wears the accent for a moment, then cools to ink in a straight line, so a short coloured wake leads the eye.

- **Build:** Words: accent={C.accent} color={C.ink} (accentOn 'all', 'first', 'last' or indices). Chain: accent="transient" (the 1.2 pace's default). Each word or fragment holds the accent accentHold after its settle (the frame it reads as landed: its rise slower than the fastest hold drift), then cools linearly over accentCool in accentSpace 'oklab' (lib/color.ts accentFade). accent="hold" keeps the last fragment in the accent for a payoff. Objects use accentFade() directly on their fill.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Words`, `fx/Chain`
- **Timing:** Hold 18 f@60 then a 13 f@60 linear cool (calm); 7 + 13 (crisp). Normal: the cool starts 3-4 f@30 after the landing and lasts 6-7 f@30.
- **Use when:** Statements building word by word, prompts typing, generated items appearing: the newest piece leads.
- **Avoid when:** The accent already means something else in the shot; long paragraphs where the wake becomes noise.

### Each word arrives on its own torn layer

`dv-torn-layer-carrier` · layout and composition · signature · energy medium · launch, sting

Each new word is printed on its own torn-paper image layer, which tears into view in stop-motion steps; the sentence builds across a stack of torn images.

- **Build:** Recipe: an SVG torn-edge mask whose reveal advances in held steps inside <Stepped>. Anatomy: Layer = image + word; the tear edge advances in 4 held steps (15, 45, 72, 100 %); layers stack. Sound: Paper tears within ±80 ms of beats. Materials: Each torn layer carries its own copy of the growing sentence, so where a new layer has torn in partway the text on it and below it sit a few pixels apart and words break across the tear (the offset = half the width of the newly added word); tear edges irregular 3-6 px with hard alpha; a new layer every 20 f.

- **Timing:** Tear steps every 10 f (30-40 f per layer), layers 50-65 f apart.
- **Use when:** A crafted, editorial film with images; a statement that grows over several pictures.
- **Avoid when:** Product UI films.
